findById, create, update, updateByHash: all return SessionMapper.toDomain(...), and create and update write through SessionMapper.toPersistence(...)

update: removes id, createdAt, updatedAt and deletedAt from the payload with `delete clonedPayload.*`; updateByHash leaves the same fields out of its type with Omit<Session, 'id' | 'createdAt' | 'updatedAt' | 'deletedAt'>. This is a small repetition inside the one class.

parsedVerdict.reasoning: The unit has one file, session.repository.ts, which holds the class SessionDocumentRepository. That class implements the SessionRepository port for Mongoose and does one job: persisting sessions in a document store. Every read is converted back to the domain model through SessionMapper.toDomain, and create and update convert to the persistence model through SessionMapper.toPersistence, so the module uses its own mapper consistently. There are two small, local quirks, and neither is a real split, duplication or bypass. First, the list of fields that can't be changed (id, createdAt, updatedAt, deletedAt) appears twice in the same class: update removes them from the payload at runtime, and updateByHash leaves them out of its payload type with Omit. Second, updateByHash writes the raw `{ hash: payload.hash }` update without going through the mapper. That is a single primitive field, so the shortcut has no practical effect. Overall the file is cohesive.
